spec.description: Wivenhoe pumped storage hydro station (Queensland) live in 3D and floor by floor: its two 285 MW reversible units in their silos, each part in the colour of what the unit is doing (generating, pumping, idle) from AEMO's five-minute SCADA, the water running down or up its penstock, and a week of pumping at midday and generating at the peaks.

spec.rawSql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
)
SELECT round(sum(pump) / 12) AS "Pumped", round(sum(gen) / 12) AS "Generated",
       round(100 * sum(gen) / nullif(sum(pump), 0)) AS "Back out"
FROM r

spec.description: Energy over the time range, from the five-minute readings (MW × 5 min): what the pumps drew from the grid to lift water up to Splityard Creek Dam, what the generators gave back, and the second as a share of the first. Over a day the upper dam may end fuller or emptier than it began, so the share swings; over the recorded week it comes near the station's round trip (about 68 % this week).
spec.title: Over the time range

spec.rawSql:
-- The newest reading of the station's four ids in the time range.
SELECT max(ts) AS time
FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}])
WHERE duid IN ('W/HOE#1', 'W/HOE#2', 'PUMP1', 'PUMP2') AND ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()

spec.description: When the newest reading in the time range was taken (AEMO stamps each reading with the end of its five-minute interval). Pacha's recorder fetches the SCADA as AEMO publishes it, every five minutes.
spec.title: Latest data

spec.rawSql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
),
latest AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE ts = (SELECT max(ts) FROM r))
SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE gen >= 5) > 0 AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE pump >= 5) > 0
            THEN 'Generating and pumping'
            WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE gen >= 5) > 0
            THEN 'Generating, ' || count(*) FILTER (WHERE gen >= 5) || ' of 2'
            WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE pump >= 5) > 0
            THEN 'Pumping, ' || count(*) FILTER (WHERE pump >= 5) || ' of 2'
            ELSE 'Idle' END AS "Doing",
       round(sum(gen) - sum(pump)) AS "Output"
FROM latest

spec.description: What Wivenhoe is doing at the end of the time range (its latest reading when the range ends now): generating, pumping or idle, and how many of its two units, from AEMO's five-minute SCADA; and the station's output, negative while it pumps (what it draws from the grid).
spec.title: The station now
About the station and the data

options.content:
Wivenhoe Power Station, between Splityard Creek Dam and Lake Wivenhoe in South East Queensland, is Queensland's only pumped storage hydro station: two reversible units of 285 MW in two concrete silos, each a pump-turbine on the shaft of a motor-generator. When power is cheap (these days around midday, while solar floods the grid) the units run as pumps and lift water some 100 m from Lake Wivenhoe up to Splityard Creek Dam; when it is dear (the morning and evening peaks) the water comes back down through the same machines, now turbines. Each unit can do either, never both at once.

On the map: every part of a unit is in the colour of what the unit was doing at the end of the time range, green generating, blue pumping, grey idle, and the water in its penstock runs down to the lake or up to the dam. The callouts chart each unit's MW over the range, pumping below zero; hover a part for its own card. The picker at the left shows one floor of the silos at a time (the hall, the generator floor, the turbine floor with the inlet valves and the penstocks, the draft tubes), the others see-through; *All* shows the whole station. Tilt and turn the map with the right button or Ctrl+drag. The brush at the top moves the time range over the recorded week: drag its window or press play to watch a day go by.

Data: [AEMO NEMweb](https://nemweb.com.au/Reports/Current/Dispatch_SCADA/), dispatch SCADA: every five minutes, each unit's output as a generator (W/HOE#1, W/HOE#2) and its pump's load (PUMP1, PUMP2), in market time (AEST, UTC+10), used under AEMO's copyright permissions; Pacha's recorder keeps about a week of it.

The model is a schematic, built by `datasets/wivenhoe/build.sh`: the hall, the transformer bays, the intake towers and the penstocks' routes are OpenStreetMap's (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL); the silos' size (about 32 m across inside) and the ratings are the station's public description (CleanCo, Wikipedia). How deep the silos go, the floors' levels, the machines' sizes, which silo is unit 1 and where the silos stand under the hall are drawn, not surveyed. There are two models, each standing on its own ground: the station by the lake, and the intake towers in Splityard Creek Dam, about 100 m up the hill. The penstocks between run along the ground on their routes, as their depth in the hill is not known, and drop down a shaft beside the hall into their silos. The ground hides nothing on the map, so only the silos and the draft tubes, under the hall and the lake, are drawn below it, under a dark see-through ground.

The base map is flat as saved. To see the hill, open the map's side panel (the arrow at its top left), go to Base map and pick *Satellite + relief*: the station, the towers, the penstocks and the callouts stand on the relief, while the floors' slabs and the dark ground do not follow it yet.

spec.rawSql:
-- The whole recording, whatever the time range: the recorder keeps about a week.
SET VARIABLE wivenhoe_week = (
  SELECT list(url) FROM (
    SELECT url FROM read_json('http://feeds/recordings/aemo-scada/manifest.json',
                              columns = {url: 'VARCHAR', "from": 'TIMESTAMPTZ', "to": 'TIMESTAMPTZ'})
    WHERE "to" >= now() - INTERVAL 8 DAY
    UNION ALL SELECT 'http://feeds/recordings/aemo-scada-empty.parquet'));
WITH s AS (
  -- The station every five minutes: both generators and both pumps.
  SELECT ts, coalesce(sum(mw) FILTER (WHERE duid IN ('W/HOE#1', 'W/HOE#2')), 0) AS gen,
             coalesce(sum(mw) FILTER (WHERE duid IN ('PUMP1', 'PUMP2')), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet(getvariable('wivenhoe_week'))
  WHERE duid IN ('W/HOE#1', 'W/HOE#2', 'PUMP1', 'PUMP2')
  GROUP BY ts
)
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 30 MINUTE, ts) AS time,
       round(avg(gen)) AS "Generating", round(avg(pump)) AS "Pumping"
FROM s
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: The whole recording (about a week) half hour by half hour: the station's mean output as a generator (green) and what its pumps drew (blue). Its window is the dashboard's time range: drag it, resize it by its handles or draw a new one, step it, or press play. The map shows the station at the window's end, the callouts and the charts the window; at the latest half hour it follows the readings as they come.
spec.title: The recorded week: pick the hours on the map

spec.rawSql:
-- The whole recording, whatever the time range: the recorder keeps about a week.
SET VARIABLE wivenhoe_week = (
  SELECT list(url) FROM (
    SELECT url FROM read_json('http://feeds/recordings/aemo-scada/manifest.json',
                              columns = {url: 'VARCHAR', "from": 'TIMESTAMPTZ', "to": 'TIMESTAMPTZ'})
    WHERE "to" >= now() - INTERVAL 8 DAY
    UNION ALL SELECT 'http://feeds/recordings/aemo-scada-empty.parquet'));
WITH s AS (
  -- The station every five minutes: both generators and both pumps.
  SELECT ts, coalesce(sum(mw) FILTER (WHERE duid IN ('W/HOE#1', 'W/HOE#2')), 0) AS gen,
             coalesce(sum(mw) FILTER (WHERE duid IN ('PUMP1', 'PUMP2')), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet(getvariable('wivenhoe_week'))
  WHERE duid IN ('W/HOE#1', 'W/HOE#2', 'PUMP1', 'PUMP2')
  GROUP BY ts
)
SELECT lpad(hour(timezone('Australia/Brisbane', ts - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE))::VARCHAR, 2, '0') || ':00' AS "Hour",
       round(avg(gen)) AS "Generating", -round(avg(pump)) AS "Pumping"
FROM s
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: The station's mean output hour by hour of the day in Brisbane time (AEST, no daylight saving), over the whole recording (about a week), whatever the time range: what the generators sent (green, up) and what the pumps drew (blue, down).

spec.rawSql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
),
latest AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE ts = (SELECT max(ts) FROM r))
-- Every part of a unit in the station (parts.parquet names them in station.glb)
-- in the colour of what its unit was doing at its latest reading in the range,
-- which the 4D Model shows; level is the part's floor, for the floor picker.
SELECT p.part, p.label AS name, p.kind, p.level, p.floor_name,
       CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END AS state,
       round(gen - pump) AS mw,
       strftime(timezone('Australia/Brisbane', ts), '%-d %b %H:%M AEST') AS reading,
       u.origin_latitude AS latitude, u.origin_longitude AS longitude
FROM latest JOIN u USING (unit)
JOIN 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/parts.parquet' p USING (unit)
WHERE p.model = 'station'
ORDER BY p.part

WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
)
-- Each unit's MW over the range for its callout, over its silo above the hall's
-- roof: generating above zero, pumping below.
SELECT r.ts AS time, u.name, round(gen - pump) AS mw,
       u.latitude, u.longitude, 24 AS altitude
FROM r JOIN u USING (unit)
ORDER BY u.unit, time

WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
),
latest AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE ts = (SELECT max(ts) FROM r))
-- Each unit's water path through the station (station-water.parquet: shaft,
-- valve, turbine, draft tube, outlet; in the station model's metres) at the end
-- of the range: generating it runs to the lake (positive), pumping back (negative).
SELECT w.name, w.model_geometry, CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END AS state,
       round(CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN gen WHEN pump >= 5 THEN -pump ELSE 0 END) AS water
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/station-water.parquet' w
LEFT JOIN latest USING (unit)
ORDER BY w.unit

-- The floors for the floor picker (floors.parquet): the ground over the station,
-- dark and see-through over all that is drawn below it, and each silo's three
-- round its machine pit; the map lifts each to its level.
SELECT level, floor_name, name, CASE WHEN level = '0' THEN 'Ground' ELSE 'Floor' END AS kind,
       geojson AS geometry
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/floors.parquet'
ORDER BY level DESC, name

WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
),
latest AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE ts = (SELECT max(ts) FROM r))
-- The intake towers in Splityard Creek Dam, a model of their own (intakes.glb)
-- standing at its own origin up the hill, in the colour of their unit.
SELECT p.part, p.label AS name, p.kind, p.level, p.floor_name,
       CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END AS state,
       round(gen - pump) AS mw,
       strftime(timezone('Australia/Brisbane', ts), '%-d %b %H:%M AEST') AS reading,
       u.intake_latitude AS latitude, u.intake_longitude AS longitude
FROM latest JOIN u USING (unit)
JOIN 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/parts.parquet' p USING (unit)
WHERE p.model = 'intakes'
ORDER BY p.part

WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
),
latest AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE ts = (SELECT max(ts) FROM r))
-- Each penstock down the hill (penstocks.parquet: from the intake tower to the
-- shaft beside the hall, in longitude and latitude, on the ground) at the end
-- of the range: generating the water runs down (positive), pumping up (negative).
SELECT k.name, k.geometry, CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END AS state,
       round(CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN gen WHEN pump >= 5 THEN -pump ELSE 0 END) AS water
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/penstocks.parquet' k
LEFT JOIN latest USING (unit)
ORDER BY k.unit

spec.description: The station in 3D over its satellite image, a schematic: the see-through machine hall on the shore of Lake Wivenhoe, and under it the two silos, one unit in each: its motor-generator, the pump-turbine in its spiral case, the inlet valve, the draft tube out to the lake, the penstock up to its intake tower in Splityard Creek Dam and its transformer. Every part in the colour of what its unit was doing at the end of the time range (green generating, blue pumping, grey idle); the water runs down to the lake while it generates and up to the dam while it pumps; each unit's callout charts its MW over the range (pumping below zero). The floor picker shows one floor of the silos at a time.
spec.title: Wivenhoe at the end of the window, floor by floor

spec.rawSql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
)
SELECT ts AS time,
       max(CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END) FILTER (WHERE unit = 1) AS "Unit 1",
       max(CASE WHEN gen >= 5 THEN 'Generating' WHEN pump >= 5 THEN 'Pumping' ELSE 'Idle' END) FILTER (WHERE unit = 2) AS "Unit 2"
FROM r
GROUP BY ts
ORDER BY ts

spec.description: Each unit every five minutes over the time range: generating (its generator reading 5 MW or more), pumping (its pump drawing 5 MW or more) or idle, from AEMO's SCADA.
spec.title: What each unit did

spec.rawSql:
WITH u AS (SELECT * FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/wivenhoe/units.parquet'),
r AS (
  -- Each unit's two readings every five minutes: as a generator (W/HOE#n) and
  -- as a pump (PUMPn, a load, positive when it draws from the grid).
  SELECT r.ts, u.unit,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.gen_duid), 0) AS gen,
         coalesce(max(r.mw) FILTER (WHERE r.duid = u.pump_duid), 0) AS pump
  FROM read_parquet([${files:singlequote}]) r JOIN u ON r.duid IN (u.gen_duid, u.pump_duid)
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY r.ts, u.unit
)
SELECT ts AS time,
       max(round(gen - pump)) FILTER (WHERE unit = 1) AS "Unit 1",
       max(round(gen - pump)) FILTER (WHERE unit = 2) AS "Unit 2"
FROM r
GROUP BY ts
ORDER BY ts
